6-1.description: Side view of a low-wing airplane. A vertical line at the leading edge of the wing is labeled "Datum (leading edge of wing)". Arrows show negative arm to the left (forward) of the datum and positive arm to the right (aft). The center of gravity symbol is marked on the fuselage, aft of the datum.

6-2.description: Side view of a low-wing airplane with the datum 40" forward of the firewall. A radio (5 lb) is 80" aft of the datum (Arm = 80"). The center of gravity is marked. A box shows: Moment = Weight (arm) = 5 lb (80") = 400 in-lb.

6-3.description: Table showing how the signs of weight and arm give the sign of the moment and the direction of rotation.
6-3.table:
| Weight | Arm | Moment | Rotation |
|---|---|---|---|
| + | + | + | Noseup |
| + | – | – | Nosedown |
| – | + | – | Nosedown |
| – | – | + | Noseup |

6-4.description: Illustration of a first class lever: a beam balanced on a fulcrum marked "Fulcrum and CG". A force 90" to the left gives Moment = 700 lb (90") = 63,000 in-lb; a force 70" to the right gives Moment = 900 lb (70") = 63,000 in-lb.

6-5.description: Illustration of finding the CG by suspending an airplane twice. 1: suspended from a first point, with a red line dropping perpendicular to the ground. 2: second suspension, with a blue line dropping perpendicular to the ground. The CG is where the red and blue lines cross.

6-6.description: Illustration of a 200" plank with the datum (0") at the left end and six weights: 50 lb at 30", 125 lb at 60", 80 lb at 95", 50 lb at 125", 90 lb at 145" and 100 lb at 170". The CG is marked at 106.9".

6-7.description: Table: CG calculation for the weights on the plank with the datum at one end (Weight × Arm = Moment).

6-8.description: Illustration of the same plank and weights with the datum (0") in the middle, the ends at –100" and 100": 50 lb at –70", 125 lb at –40", 80 lb at –5", 50 lb at 25", 90 lb at 45" and 100 lb at 70". The CG is marked at 6.9".

6-13.description: Excerpt titled "Comprehensive Equipment List" from a Cessna Model 182S Pilot's Operating Handbook. It explains the list's columns: the Item No (the first two digits are the ATA iSpec 2200 chapter, then a sequence number and a suffix letter: –R required items or equipment for FAA certification, –S standard equipment items, –O optional equipment items replacing required or standard items, –A optional equipment items in addition to required or standard items); the Equipment List Description; the Ref Drawing; and the Wt Lbs and Arm Ins columns. Notes say that additional equipment must be installed per the reference drawing, a service bulletin or a separate FAA approval; that positive arms are distances aft of the airplane datum and negative arms forward of it; and that asterisks in the weight and arm columns mark complete assembly installations.

6-14.description: Two pages of Type Certificate Data Sheet No. A7SO (Piper PA-34-200 Seneca and later models, Revision 19), with weight and balance items highlighted in yellow: the engine limits, the C.G. range (gear extended), the empty weight C.G. range (None) and the maximum weight.

6-15.description: Four pages of TCDS A7SO with weight and balance items highlighted, labeled A: fuel capacity (98 gallons), engine limits, number of seats, maximum baggage, oil capacity, C.G. range and maximum weight.

6-16.description: Two pages of TCDS A7SO with highlighted items: NOTE 1 (the current weight and balance report and the fuel and oil included in certificated empty weight) and, under Data Pertinent to All Models, the datum and the leveling means.

6-18.description: Photograph of a Cessna 182 with its nose wheel and main wheels (in fairings) resting on portable electronic platform scales.

6-19.description: Photograph of a digital scale indicator in a yellow carrying case, with a red display, function keys and a numeric keypad.

6-20.description: Photograph of a technician working a blue tripod jack placed under a jack point on the underside of a jet, next to its main landing gear. A load cell sits on top of the jack.

6-21.description: Photograph of hands holding a spirit level against the side of a Mooney M20 fuselage, with an inset of the level's bubble.

6-22.description: Photograph of a plumb bob hanging on a string from the wing leading edge down to the hangar floor, next to the main wheel.

6-23.description: Photograph of two people under an airplane measuring with a tape measure from the nose wheel scale to a point on the floor.

6-24.description: Text box from the TCDS: "CG Range: (Gear Extended) S/N 34-E4, 34-7250001 through 34-7250214 (See NOTE 3) (+86.4") to (+94.6") at 4,000 lb, (+82.0") to (+94.6") at 3,400 lb, (+80.7") to (+94.6") at 2,780 lb. 6-25.description: Graph of the Piper Seneca CG envelope: weight (lb) from 2,600 to 4,200 on the vertical axis and center of gravity (in) from 78 to 98 on the horizontal axis. The forward CG limit runs straight up at 80.7 to 2,780 lb (red), then slopes through 82 at 3,400 lb (blue) to 86.4 at 4,000 lb (green). The maximum weight line runs across at 4,000 lb (orange) to the aft CG limit, a vertical line at 94.6.

Labels: nose scale reading 225 lb, right scale reading 640 lb, left scale reading 650 lb, chocks, nosewheel centerline, main wheel centerline, and wheel base. The main wheel centerline is 70" from the datum and the wheel base is 100".

6-42.description: Diagram of a lever: a ballast weight of 46.68 lb at an arm of 60" on the left and the aircraft weight of 3,034 lb at a CG of 99.6" on the right. The distance from the aft limit to the ballast is 39" and the CG is 0.6" out of limits. A note reads: "In order to balance at the aft limit of 99", the moment to the left of the fulcrum must equal the moment to the right of the fulcrum. The moment to the right is the weight of the airplane multiplied by 0.6". The moment to the left is the ballast weight multiplied by 39"."

A "Weight and Balance Calculation" table has columns Item, Scale (lb), Tare Wt. (lb), Net Wt. (lb), Arm (inches) and Moment (in-lb), with rows Nose, Tail, Left Main, Right Main, Subtotal, Fuel, Oil, Misc. and Total.
